answer: Like a meadow that only lets a few boats dock at its jetty at a time, a market can cap new agents with a probationary throughput limit and a refundable stake deposit. Each agent locks tokens before transacting; the deposit is slashed on proven fraud and refunded after a clean history. Reputation decays, so an attacker cannot farm one good record and echo it across a thousand fresh identities — every new identity pays the deposit and the waiting cost again, making a sybil swarm far more expensive than the value it can extract.
